title: [spec-gap][R-CCP12-001/018] Normative channel-selection priority chain contradicted: spec §1 vs §6 vs implementations
description: Sweep docs/spec-coverage/appendix-ccp12-hopping.md. Spec §1 priority table: 1=announce CCP-9, 2=hash CCP-16, 3=synchronized hop CCP-12, 4=CH0. Spec §6 pseudocode: announce → hash(density>10→CH0 inside) → CH0, no CCP-12 step. Actual chains: python link/channel.py:112-158 = announce → GNSS-synced CCP-12 → hash(eui64+epoch+sfn, no density) → CH0 (tested test_channel.py:217-278 incl. test_announce_beats_gnss_synced); rust lib.rs:165-201 = GNSS → hash → CH0. So: spec self-contradicts (§1 vs §6) and both stacks contradict both. Density check exists only in python channel_plan.py — a GNSS-synced node never falls back to CH0 under density>10 in any chain implementation. Rendezvous interop requires one normative chain. Suggested: adjudicate the intended order (implemented order is defensible: locked sync beats epoch rendezvous), amend §1/§6, and specify whether/how density>10 overrides GNSS-synced selection.
